text: My name is Greta Thunberg.
I am 15 years old and I'm from Sweden.
I speak on behalf of climate justice now.
Many people say that Sweden is just a small country and it doesn't matter what we do.
But I've learned that you are never too small to make a difference.
note: Contrast to previous sentence, personal learning, punchline

text: And if a few children can get headlines all over the world just by not going to school, then imagine what we could all do together if we really wanted to.
note: Sets up hypothetical, invites imagination of collective action

text: But to do that, we have to speak clearly, no matter how uncomfortable that may be.
You only speak of green, eternal economic growth because you are too scared of being unpopular.
note: Accusation of leaders' fear of unpopularity

text: You only talk about moving forward
with the same bad ideas that got us into this mess, even when the only sensible thing to do is pull the emergency brake.
You are not mature enough to tell it like it is.
Even that burden you leave to us children.
But I don't care about being popular.
note: Contrast to leaders' popularity concern, personal testimony

text: I care about climate justice and a living planet.
Our civilization is being sacrificed for the opportunity of a very small number of people to continue making enormous amounts of money.
note: Accusation of civilization sacrifice for profit

text: Our biosphere is being sacrificed so that rich people in countries like mine can live in luxury.
It is the sufferings of the many which pay for the luxuries of the few.
The year 2078
I will celebrate my 75th birthday.
If I have children, maybe they will spend that day with me.
Maybe they will ask me about you.
Maybe they will ask why you didn't do anything while there still was time to act.
note: Direct address, rhetorical question, accusation of future inaction

text: You say you love your children above all else, and yet you're stealing their future in front of their very eyes.
note: Contrast between words and actions, accusation, punchline

text: Until you start focusing on what needs to be done, rather than what is politically possible, there is no hope.
note: Contrast 'needs to be done' vs 'politically possible', warning of no hope

text: We cannot solve a crisis without treating it as a crisis.
We need to keep the fossil fuels in the ground and we need to focus on equity.
And if solutions within this system are so impossible to find, then maybe we should change the system itself.
note: Puzzle/solution, punchline, call for systemic change

text: We have not come here to beg world leaders to care.
note: Sets up a contrast, statement of defiance

text: You have ignored us in the past and you will ignore us again.
note: Accusation of past and future inaction

text: We have run out of excuses and we are running out of time.
We have come here to let you know that change is coming, whether you like it or not.
The real power belongs to the people.
Thank you.
you
